AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Vancomycin is very commonly used in combination with piperacillin-tazobactam (PTZ) as an initial empiric therapy for moderate to severe infections, whenever coverage for both methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa is required. The combination of vancomycin and PTZ in adults has recently been reported to significantly increase the risk of developing acute kidney injury (AKI) relative to vancomycin monotherapy; such reports in pediatrics are sparse.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Retrospective chart review of pediatric patients, aged 0-14 years, who were admitted to general wards or ICU and developed AKI after receiving vancomycin and PTZ concomitantly for more than 48 hours. AKI has been defined as a decrease in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) by 50% or more from baseline. Cases were identified by reviewing the Adverse Drug Reaction program database at King Saud University Medical City in Saudi Arabia from January 2015 to June 2016.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Eight cases of drug induced nephrotoxicity have occurred in children who were admitted to the hospital and received concomitant therapy with vancomycin and PTZ for treatment of pneumonia (seven patients) or febrile neutropenia (one patient). Application of the Drug Interaction Probability Scale (DIPS) for causation assessment resulted in a score of 9 for all cases (highly probable).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Caution in utilizing the combination of vancomycin and PTZ is warranted in pediatrics as well. Healthcare professionals should practice increased vigilance if this combination is to be initiated with close monitoring for renal function. Antibiotic therapy de-escalation should be considered as soon as culture results are available. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
